title: PaymentSession
description: A PaymentIntent (ADR-014) presented through one or more interfaces (ADR-015). The PaymentIntent is the single financial object; the session is the rule binding its interfaces (Payment Link, Dynamic QR, Static QR, Deep Link) to one destination, one currency, one amount-when-fixed, one expiry, one idempotency policy, and one financial result. `session_id` is the PaymentIntent id. The destination MAY be a segregated Wallet Account (ADR-020). An interface never changes the destination or amount; payment always resolves against the session, at the operator. Applications display the interfaces; they never generate an authoritative financial payload and never compute a destination.

session_id.description: The PaymentIntent id (ADR-014). Non-enumerable. Every interface resolves to this.

operator_id.description: The operator that owns and resolves the session.

owner_ref.description: The session owner (e.g. the payee). Opaque to the protocol.

destination_account_ref.description: Optional segregated Wallet Account (ADR-020) to credit — e.g. a campaign account. Absent ⇒ the payee wallet's default account. Resolved by the operator; never exposes an internal ledger account id to apps.

purpose.description: Operator/app purpose tag (e.g. DONATION, ORDER, TICKET). Opaque to the protocol.

reference_id.description: Opaque app reference id (e.g. a campaign id).

amount_minor.description: Fixed amount in integer minor units; null for open-amount sessions. Never float.

status.description: Session status (mirrors the PaymentIntent; PARTIALLY_PAID only where the operator supports partial collection). An interface state may differ but MUST NOT contradict this.

expires_at.description: Session expiry. Shared by every interface; an interface MAY expire earlier but not later.

interfaces.description: The interfaces presenting this session. Each conforms to payment-session-interface.schema.json. At least one.

metadata.description: Operator/app metadata. Opaque to the protocol.

_numeric_domain: Integers in a signed or digested BANZA artifact are bounded by the canonicalization in force (BCJ/1: |n| <= 2^53-1, spec/canonicalization.md P2). The bound is declared here so the schema and the canonicalization cannot disagree about what is representable.
